authoritative_for: repository dataset counts and normalization status

hanja.semantic_derivation: mechanically split comma-delimited libhangul meaning_ko after deduplicating exact reading-character relations

myeongri.status: structured fixed tables + KASI boundary vectors + pinned independent implementation crosscheck; Korea-specific full-pillar golden set still pending

notes: README files should reference this file instead of maintaining independent counts.
U+25874 is present in the character master but has no reading in the secondary mirror.
Traditional naming stroke counts must not be inferred from Unicode kTotalStrokes.
Surname core data now covers 2015 census ranks 1-31 (31 records total); the user-requested expansion file contains 30 records excluding already-built 徐(rank 13).
representative-clans-2015.csv is a partial official representative-clan table, not a complete bongwan list for each surname.
All 31 core surnames now have curated clan/genealogy research rows with evidence levels; this does not mean every clan or hangnyeol line is complete.
clans-core-2015.csv uses up to 7 selected major bongwan plus a computed remainder per surname; it is an exact-to-total summary, not a full copy of every 5+ person KOSIS bongwan row.
Hanja can have multiple documented senses. meaning-senses.csv preserves all split senses by (hanja, legal_reading); naming interpretations are a separate editorial layer.
Selected naming sense, naming intent, and semantic-risk notices are separate from dictionary senses; semantic risk is not a fortune score and only invalid evidence/readings are blocked by default.
Core Hanja normalization/index/semantic-sense files and source-audit.csv have exact regeneration scripts checked by CI.
2026 and 2027 solar-term rows were verified against KASI calendar/almanac pages on 2026-11-14.
Every registered external source has a machine-readable rights/use classification in data/meta/source-rights.csv; unverified sources default to reference/summary-only handling.
Naming semantic curation reached 300 characters / 652 reviewed sense rows; this is an editorial priority core, not an official popularity ranking.
Seven suspicious semantic source rows are explicitly held for source recheck rather than silently corrected.
48 KASI-backed month-branch boundary vectors cover the exact minute before/at each 2026-2027 monthly start solar term.

lunar-python 1.4.9 crosscheck found its solar-term table is Beijing-time based; raw Korean local-clock fields switch month branch about one hour earlier than KASI Korea-local boundaries, so the library output is not treated as Korean golden truth.

Common onset pronunciation-five-elements mapping now has 14 source-bound basic consonant rows; tense-consonant normalization remains intentionally unsupported until a method-specific source is registered.
The 81-row numerology table previously hardcoded in knolname is preserved as legacy_knolname_v0_2_0 with authoritative_for_scoring=false; it is regression evidence, not a verified numerology source.

knolname2 server/dataLoader.ts resource-element 214-radical map, 84 semantic overrides, and 11 wonhoek delta rules are now preserved in data/methods as explicit non-authoritative legacy method tables.

Unihan kRSKangXi radical number + residual stroke data now has a source-bound 17-range Kangxi radical stroke reconstruction method; this replaces ad-hoc delta patches for technical reconstruction but is not automatically a universal naming-school wonhoek standard.
Kumasaki and Cai Shen/Hongfan 81-number traditions are registered as separate historical methods; KCI 2019 reports 27/81 opposing good/bad judgments, so no universal 81 table is claimed.

Court name-statistics reuse policy is verified for court-owned public works with specific source attribution; exact normalized birth/rename snapshots still require direct query extraction with scope/date metadata.
Fourteen naming-method records are now separated, with 21 evidence-role rows and 14 readiness rows; no method is marked final_scoring_ready.
The irrelevant 2011 auricular-acupuncture voice-signal paper was removed from pronunciation-five-elements evidence; pronunciation sources now come from directly relevant naming studies.
Labial/guttural pronunciation-five-elements conflict is explicit: the stored common variant and a Haerye-based alternative are separate methods rather than silently merged.
Official court birth-name and rename-name statistics have a validated snapshot schema and ingestion policy; direct official TOP20 values remain pending extraction.
